extracted.intended_audience: comedians, performers and show producers planning to enter or be considered for comedy awards at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility and judging criteria for the various comedy-related awards run (or run independently) during the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, including entry instructions, categories, and how winners are chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedians' Choice Awards — Best Show / Best Newcomer / Best Person eligibility & voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Show, Best Newcomer and Best Person, as determined by those involved in comedy shows. All comedy shows and performers are automatically eligible for Best Show and Best Newcomer. Best Person tends to be for someone who works behind the scenes at the festival (eg a venue manager, flyerer or agent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each comedy show in the brochure is invited to vote once for their favourite show, performer and person. You can't vote for anyone in your own show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy Poster Awards — poster eligibility and award types
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognises the best artwork related to comedy shows at the festival. Any poster related to a comedy show performing at the festival can be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are two awards: an Audience Award (the poster with the most votes on the website) and a Panel Award (determined by a jury of industry professionals). Winners are offered future poster placements from distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edinburgh Comedy Awards — Best Comic/Comedy Show & Best Newcomer criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Two awards: Best Comic / Comedy Show (funniest, most outstanding, up-and-coming comic/comedy show/act) with a £10,000 prize; Best Newcomer (performer or act performing their first full-length show of 50 minutes or more) with a £5,000 prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newcomers are eligible for the Best Comedy Show Award if the Panel decides, but no act can appear on both shortlists in the same year. For full eligibility rules see the awards site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edinburgh Comedy Awards — eligibility checking and judging process
rubrics_metrics.description: All shows listed in the comedy and cabaret section of the Fringe brochure are automatically checked for eligibility. Shows needed to be playing the dates as outlined in the eligibility rules in order to be judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible shows are seen by the judging panel, awards administration team and scouts, who start covering shows from the first day of the festival. The judging panel consists of comedy critics, industry professionals (TV and live) and punter judges; scouts are previous members of the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victoria Wood Award (Panel Prize) — open/subjective Panel Prize
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Prize: Like the Fringe itself, there are no rules. Everyone is eligible. It is entirely in the gift of the Panel and Award Director and may not be awarded at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize amount is listed (£5,000); awarding is discretionary and not governed by specific eligibility beyond being under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edinburgh Fringe Comedian of the Year — format and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual search selecting 100 of the best comedians at the Fringe to compete for audience votes, the title, trophy, and a cash prize (£1,500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comedians are eligible. Comedians who fail to win heats/semi-finals have one more chance via wildcards; all shows are recorded and posted to YouTube and the online audience can vote for wildcard entries. Applicants must email to receive an application form by a specified closing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Comedy & Edinburgh Fringe Awards — performer residency/Europe-based eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Two awards to showcase European comedy talent (Best European Comedy Performer and Best European Comedy Show) and provide paid performance opportunities abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires the performer to have either: started comedy in Europe (for more than two years), been based in Europe while performing (for more than two years), or currently be based in Europe (for more than one year). Winners receive travel/lodging and performance opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISH Edinburgh Comedy Awards — volunteer-run prize distribution and category types
rubrics_metrics.description: Run entirely by volunteers; 100% of whatever sponsorship is received will be given to artists in prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple categories (Best Show, Best Newcomer, tech awards, etc.) exist; full eligibility criteria and details are provided on the awards' own site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Thieves World Championship — performance rules and entrant types
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition for performers who adapt to performing opponents' jokes/sketches with zero preparation time; entrants must only perform their opponents' material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch performers/groups, stand-up comedians and musical comedians are all eligible. The format emphasises improvisational skill and adaptability rather than original material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malcolm Hardee Awards — spontaneous nomination & category definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories (Comic Originality, Cunning Stunt and Act That Should Make A Million Quid). No application process; judges proactively seek nominees across the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards celebrate madcap, anarchic, originality and stunt-based publicity. Judges scour the festival looking for nominees without formal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NextUp Biggest Award in Comedy — competition purpose and prize
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition run by NextUp to find the best comedy show at the Fringe. Winner receives a large inflatable trophy, cash, and option for global recording/distribution by NextUp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize package includes physical trophy, pump and carry case, £500 cash, and possible recording/distribution; entry/judging mechanics are run by NextUp.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Some guy called) DAVE Joke of the Fringe — one-liner submission & selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual search for the best one-liners at the Fringe. Comedians with shows can submit up to five one-liners from their shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are shortlisted by industry professionals to a longlist of 25; an external group of Fringe-goers pick a top 10 from which the winning joke is chosen. Comedians in the top 10 may be invited to perform paid showcases. Eligibility requires performing own solo show or being a named performer on a split-bill show.

rubrics_metrics.name: So You Think You’re Funny? — newcomer eligibility and round format
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition to discover new comic talent with historically strict newcomer criteria. Entrants must not have performed more than 15 stand-up spots (including open spots and virtual performances to live audiences) or gigged before a specified cutoff date, and must be unsigned by any comedy agent or management company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each competitor is given seven minutes in heats; heat winners progress to a Grand Final. Prizes include cash, festival runs, paid festival slots, professional photos/video, and mentorship. Full rules are on the competition's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amused Moose Comedy Awards — 'almost television-ready' breakthrough criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks breakthrough comedy talent that is close to being 'television-ready' with a solo, sketch or multiple performer comedy show at the Fringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award targets acts that are at the cusp of wider exposure/TV suitability; entrants must have a relevant show at the Fringe. Full details may be provided when the award runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Takeover Radio / Other 'Joke of the Fringe' style awards — submission limits and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Various joke/one-liner awards (e.g., Takeover Radio 106.9FM Joke of the Fringe, U&Dave's Joke of the Fringe) run annual searches for best jokes with submission limits and selection processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical process: comedians submit jokes by deadline; industry professionals longlist; final selection may involve audience voting or invited performances. Note: some iterations may be cancelled in a given year.
